messages.author: deb55ea526b6a46e
messages.subject: Remove gray gridlines
parts:
ggplot2 community,

I am producing a figure for publication and would like to remove the gray grid lines from the plot [these are present after using theme_bw()].  I have found numerous methods for doing this but they seem to not actually remove the grid lines or are broken/deprecated.   

As version 0.9.0 has many new bells and whistles I figured I'd ask here to get the easiest way to approach the suppression of grid lines.  Here is my reproducible code:
library(ggplot2)
x <- ggplot(CO2, aes(x=uptake, group=Plant))
y <- x + geom_density(aes(colour=Plant)) + facet_grid(Type~Treatment)
y + theme_bw()


Here is a link to the example code in case the formatting of this email is messed up.
http://dl.dropbox.com/u/61803503/script.txt

Thank you in advance,
Tyler

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Remove gray gridlines
parts:
Hi Tyler:

You might want to consider the use of theming your ggplot2 graphics if
you want a consistent style (or set of styles) for use in a paper or
other type of document. This link shows a number of themes created by
ggplot2 users: https://github.com/hadley/ggplot2/wiki/themes/ Also
see the theme_nothing() function in the ggmap package. You may well be
able to pick and choose what you (don't) want by looking at these
examples and using them for inspiration.

HTH,
Dennis
